Orphograph offline verifier kit
================================

Python 3.11 or later required. No installation, no internet, no
account, no third-party packages.

To verify a single file against an inclusion proof:

  python3 verify.py file --file YOUR_FILE --proof PROOF.json --ots ROOT.ots

To re-hash a whole folder and check it matches a folder receipt:

  python3 verify.py folder --dir YOUR_FOLDER --manifest MANIFEST.json --ots ROOT.ots

If the folder was anchored with custom exclude patterns, pass the same
repeatable --exclude GLOB flags here (any --exclude replaces the default
deny-list); with different excludes the recomputed root cannot match.

Everything above is STRUCTURAL: hashes are recomputed and compared
locally, and no network call is made. It does not consult Bitcoin.

The optional --ots argument is the chain step. It runs the public
OpenTimestamps client, and reports THAT client's verdict — not ours.

Two things to know before relying on it:

  * `ots verify` needs a Bitcoin node it can reach. It does not fall
    back to a block explorer. Without a node (tested against client
    v0.7.2) it exits non-zero with "Could not connect to Bitcoin
    node", and this verifier reports UNAVAILABLE — meaning the check
    did not run. UNAVAILABLE is NOT a statement that your timestamp
    is bad, and it is never treated as success.
  * PENDING means the calendars hold the attestation but Bitcoin has
    not confirmed it yet. Also not success.

If `ots` is not installed the verifier still recomputes the Merkle
tree and compares it to the recorded root; the chain check can be
re-run later from any machine with the client and a node.

    pip install opentimestamps-client
    ots info  <file>.ots     # read the attestation offline, no node

The script source is short enough to read in one sitting. It depends
only on the Python standard library.

Anchor receipts issued by the Orphograph office can be re-verified
forever using only this kit, the original files, and a Bitcoin node
(or any block explorer). Verification does not require contacting
the office.
